question:
The grouped data for the observation are

 
 

 Class:
 1-3
 3-5
 5-7
 
 

 Frequency:
 2
 1
 2
 
 

The population skewness
solution:
The correct answer **is zero**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Population skewness** measures the asymmetry of a population distribution.
 
• A value of zero indicates a symmetric distribution.
 
• The** formula for population** skewness is given as: Skewness = 3 * (Mean - Median) / Standard Deviation
 
• **Skewness** is one of the measures of shape and central tendency.
 
• Other measures such as kurtosis and standard deviation are also important in understanding the overall distribution of data.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The population skewness measures the asymmetry of a population distribution, with a value of zero indicating a symmetric distribution. The formula for population skewness is given as:
 
 
• Skewness = 3 * (Mean - Median) / Standard Deviation
 
 
 
• In a grouped data set, the standard deviation cannot be calculated, hence the skewness is only estimated.
 
 
• However, in this case, the observation of equal frequencies in two of the classes suggests that the distribution is symmetric and the skewness is close to zero.
 
 
 
• It's important to note that skewness is one of the measures of shape and central tendency and can help us understand the distribution of data
 
 
• however it's not the only one and other measures such as kurtosis and standard deviation are also important in understanding the overall distribution of data.
